meta.title: AUD Area IV - Forming Conclusions and Reporting
meta.blueprint: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints, AUD (Approved by the Board of Examiners Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026); copy hosted at dokoblog.com (third party host of the AICPA PDF)

items.topic: Structure of an unmodified auditor's report (nonissuer)
items.task: Identify the appropriate form and content of an auditor's report.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: In an unmodified report on the financial statements of a nonissuer under AICPA standards, which sections come first and second?
options: A Responsibilities of Management section first, then Auditor's Responsibilities
An introductory paragraph first, followed by a scope paragraph and then the opinion
A Basis for Opinion section first, followed by an Opinion section
An Opinion section first, followed by a Basis for Opinion section
items.rule_line: The current report begins with the Opinion section, then Basis for Opinion, then other sections.

why.A: The management and auditor responsibility sections follow the opinion and basis sections.
why.B: That describes the older report format, not the current format.
why.C: The order is reversed; the opinion is presented first.
why.D: Correct. The first section contains the opinion, and the second is the basis for opinion.

guide.ask: In the current unmodified report format, what leads the report?
guide.reveal: The opinion itself.

guide.ask: What follows it?
guide.reveal: The basis for opinion, so the opinion section is first and the basis second.

items.topic: Qualified opinion for a material but not pervasive misstatement
items.task: Identify the types of opinions and the form and content of a modified report.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: The auditor of Redcliff Tools, a nonissuer, concludes that inventory is overstated by an amount that is material to the balance sheet and income statement but is not pervasive to the financial statements. Management will not correct it. Which opinion is appropriate?
options: A disclaimer of opinion, stating that the auditor does not express an opinion
A qualified opinion, worded as except for the effects of the matter described in the basis section
An unmodified opinion with an emphasis-of-matter paragraph describing the inventory error
An adverse opinion, stating that the financial statements do not present fairly
items.rule_line: Material but not pervasive misstatement: qualified opinion; material and pervasive: adverse opinion.

why.A: A disclaimer applies when the auditor cannot obtain sufficient appropriate evidence and the possible effects are pervasive.
why.B: Correct. A material but not pervasive misstatement results in a qualified opinion, worded as except for the effects of the matter.
why.C: An emphasis-of-matter paragraph cannot be used to avoid modifying the opinion for a material misstatement.
why.D: An adverse opinion applies when misstatements are both material and pervasive.

guide.ask: Is the inventory misstatement material and pervasive?
guide.reveal: Material, but not pervasive.

guide.ask: Which opinion follows?
guide.reveal: A qualified opinion, worded as except for the effects of the matter.

items.topic: Disclaimer of opinion for pervasive scope limitation
items.task: Identify the types of opinions and the appropriate report for a scope limitation.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: A fire destroyed the accounting records of Sierra Freight, a nonissuer, and the auditor cannot obtain sufficient appropriate evidence about revenue, receivables, inventory and payables. The auditor concludes that the possible effects of undetected misstatements could be both material and pervasive. What should the auditor do?
options: Disclaim an opinion on the financial statements, or withdraw from the audit when practicable
Express an adverse opinion, because the financial statements cannot be relied upon
Express a qualified opinion, using the phrase except for the possible effects of the matters described
Express an unmodified opinion and add an emphasis-of-matter paragraph about the fire
items.rule_line: Inability to obtain evidence with material and pervasive possible effects leads to a disclaimer or withdrawal.

why.A: Correct. When the auditor cannot obtain evidence and the possible effects are material and pervasive, the auditor disclaims an opinion or withdraws when practicable.
why.B: An adverse opinion is for misstatements the auditor has concluded exist and are material and pervasive, not for an inability to obtain evidence.
why.C: A qualified opinion is for possible effects that are material but not pervasive.
why.D: An emphasis-of-matter paragraph cannot be used in place of modifying the opinion.

guide.ask: Can the auditor obtain sufficient evidence on the affected accounts?
guide.reveal: No, the records were destroyed.

guide.ask: What follows when possible effects are material and pervasive?
guide.reveal: Disclaim an opinion, or withdraw when practicable.

items.topic: Emphasis-of-matter paragraph
items.task: Identify when to include emphasis-of-matter and other-matter paragraphs.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: Note 12 to the financial statements of Cobalt Freight, a nonissuer, appropriately discloses a major plant fire after year-end that is fundamental to users' understanding of the statements. The auditor concludes that no modification of the opinion is needed. What should the auditor include in the report?
options: An emphasis-of-matter paragraph in a separate section, referring to note 12 and stating the opinion is not modified
A qualified opinion, because an event this significant to users of the financial statements requires a modification
An other-matter paragraph describing the fire in detail using information that is not in the notes
A statement in the Basis for Opinion section only, with no separate section or reference
items.rule_line: An emphasis-of-matter paragraph refers only to matters disclosed in the statements and states that the opinion is not modified.

why.A: Correct. An emphasis-of-matter paragraph draws attention to a matter properly disclosed, refers to the note, and states that the opinion is not modified.
why.B: A properly disclosed matter does not require a modified opinion.
why.C: An emphasis-of-matter paragraph may refer only to information presented or disclosed in the financial statements.
why.D: The paragraph must be in a separate section with an appropriate heading.

guide.ask: Is the fire properly disclosed, and does it require modifying the opinion?
guide.reveal: Properly disclosed and no modification needed.

guide.ask: What does the report add to draw attention to it?
guide.reveal: A separate emphasis-of-matter paragraph that refers to note 12 and states the opinion is not modified.

items.topic: Reporting on substantial doubt about going concern (nonissuer)
items.task: Report on an entity's ability to continue as a going concern.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: The auditor of Harbor Lane Foods, a nonissuer, concludes that substantial doubt about the entity's ability to continue as a going concern remains after considering management's plans, and the financial statement disclosures are adequate. What should the auditor's report include?
options: A disclaimer of opinion, because future events cannot be predicted
A separate section about substantial doubt that draws attention to the note and states the opinion is not modified
A sentence in the Basis for Opinion section that does not refer to the note
An adverse opinion, because substantial doubt exists about the entity's ability to continue as a going concern for a year
items.rule_line: Remaining substantial doubt with adequate disclosure: separate section, attention to the note, opinion not modified.

why.A: A disclaimer is not required when the auditor can form an opinion on the statements.
why.B: Correct. With adequate disclosure and remaining substantial doubt, the report has a separate section that draws attention to the note and states the opinion is not modified.
why.C: The section must draw attention to the note that discloses the conditions and management's plans.
why.D: An adverse opinion applies if the going concern basis is inappropriate, not when doubt exists and the basis is appropriate.

guide.ask: Are the disclosures adequate despite the doubt?
guide.reveal: Yes, so no modification is needed.

guide.ask: What does the report contain?
guide.reveal: A separate section on substantial doubt that draws attention to the note and states the opinion is not modified.

items.topic: Critical audit matters in an issuer's report
items.task: Identify the form and content of an auditor's report for an issuer.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: In the audit of an issuer, which matter is a critical audit matter under PCAOB standards?
options: A departure from GAAP that caused the auditor to qualify the opinion on the financial statements
A properly disclosed matter that the auditor believes is fundamental to users' understanding of the statements
A matter communicated to the audit committee, relating to material items, that involved especially challenging judgment
Any matter discussed with management during the audit that led to a significant adjustment to the financial statements
items.rule_line: A critical audit matter was communicated to the audit committee, relates to material items, and involved especially challenging judgment.

why.A: Critical audit matters are not a substitute for a modified opinion, which addresses departures from GAAP.
why.B: That describes an emphasis paragraph, not a critical audit matter.
why.C: Correct. This is the definition of a critical audit matter.
why.D: Discussion with management and adjustments do not define a critical audit matter; the matter must have been communicated to the audit committee and involve challenging judgment.

guide.ask: What is a critical audit matter?
guide.reveal: A matter communicated to the audit committee, relating to material accounts or disclosures, that involved especially challenging, subjective or complex judgment.

guide.ask: Which choice matches that definition?
guide.reveal: The one describing a communicated matter with especially challenging judgment.

items.topic: Key audit matters in a nonissuer report
items.task: Identify the appropriate form and content of a report, including key audit matters.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: When must the auditor of a nonissuer communicate key audit matters in the auditor's report under AICPA standards?
options: In every audit of the financial statements of any nonissuer client
Only when the auditor expresses a modified opinion on the statements
Only when the client is a not-for-profit organization or a plan
When the auditor has been engaged to communicate key audit matters
items.rule_line: For nonissuers, key audit matters are communicated when the auditor is engaged to do so.

why.A: Key audit matters are not required in every nonissuer audit.
why.B: Key audit matters and modified opinions are unrelated; a modification does not trigger the requirement.
why.C: The nature of the entity does not determine the requirement; the engagement does.
why.D: Correct. Communication of key audit matters is required when the auditor is engaged to do so.

guide.ask: When are key audit matters communicated under AICPA standards?
guide.reveal: Only when the auditor is engaged to do so.

guide.ask: Is it required in every audit or modified opinion?
guide.reveal: No.

items.topic: Dating the auditor's report
items.task: Determine the date of the auditor's report.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: Fieldwork for the audit of Bellamy Corp., a nonissuer, ended on February 18, 2026. The financial statements and all notes were completed on February 22, and management asserted that it took responsibility for them on February 24. The representation letter is dated February 24. Which is the earliest date the auditor may date the report?
options: February 18, 2026
February 22, 2026
February 24, 2026
February 26, 2026
items.rule_line: The report date is no earlier than the date sufficient evidence exists, including that statements are complete and management has taken responsibility.

why.A: This is the end of fieldwork, before the statements were completed and management took responsibility.
why.B: The statements were complete on this date, but management had not yet asserted responsibility.
why.C: Correct. The report may not be dated before the auditor has evidence that all statements and disclosures were prepared and that management asserted responsibility for them, which occurred on February 24.
why.D: This date is later than necessary; nothing requires waiting beyond February 24.

guide.ask: What must the auditor have before dating the report?
guide.reveal: Evidence that all statements and disclosures were prepared and that management asserted responsibility for them.

guide.ask: Which is the first date when both are met?
guide.reveal: February 24, 2026.

items.topic: Conclusion in an examination report
items.task: Identify the factors for reporting on examination and review engagements.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: A practitioner performs an assertion-based examination of Everly Energy's statement of greenhouse gas emissions under the attestation standards. What does the practitioner's report express?
options: A conclusion, based on limited assurance, about whether material modifications are needed
An opinion based on reasonable assurance about whether the statement meets the criteria
A statement that no assurance is provided on the statement of emissions and that no procedures were performed
A summary of procedures performed and findings, with no opinion or conclusion on the subject matter at all
items.rule_line: An examination gives an opinion based on reasonable assurance; a review gives a conclusion based on limited assurance.

why.A: That describes a review engagement.
why.B: Correct. An examination provides reasonable assurance and results in an opinion.
why.C: That describes a preparation-type service without assurance, not an attest examination.
why.D: That describes an agreed-upon procedures engagement.

guide.ask: What level of assurance does an examination provide?
guide.reveal: Reasonable assurance.

guide.ask: What does the report express?
guide.reveal: An opinion.

items.topic: Content of an agreed-upon procedures report
items.task: Identify factors for reporting on agreed-upon procedures engagements.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: A practitioner completes an agreed-upon procedures engagement for Kilburn Foods on trade promotion payments. Which must the report include?
options: The procedures performed and the findings from each, and a statement that the report may not suit other purposes
Management's assertion about the trade promotion payments, with the practitioner's assurance on that assertion
An opinion on whether the trade promotion payment schedule is fairly stated in all material respects
An overall conclusion on whether the payments conform to the specified criteria for trade promotion payments
items.rule_line: An agreed-upon procedures report describes procedures and findings and gives no opinion or conclusion.

why.A: Correct. The report is in the form of procedures and findings and states the purpose and that it may not be suitable for other purposes.
why.B: The report does not provide assurance on management's assertion.
why.C: An opinion is provided by an examination, not by agreed-upon procedures.
why.D: The practitioner may not express an opinion or conclusion in an agreed-upon procedures report.

guide.ask: What form does an agreed-upon procedures report take?
guide.reveal: Procedures performed and findings from each, with no opinion.

guide.ask: What else must it state?
guide.reveal: Its purpose and that it may not suit other purposes.

items.topic: Independence in an agreed-upon procedures engagement
items.task: Identify factors for reporting on agreed-upon procedures engagements.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: A CPA who is not independent of a client is asked to perform an agreed-upon procedures engagement under the attestation standards. No law or regulation requires the CPA to accept the engagement. Which statement is correct?
options: The CPA may perform the engagement if the CPA is objective, whether or not independent
The CPA may perform the engagement if the report states that the CPA is not independent, even though no law requires it
The CPA may perform the engagement, because independence is not required in agreed-upon procedures engagements
The CPA may not perform it, because independence is required unless law or regulation requires acceptance
items.rule_line: A practitioner must be independent for an attest engagement unless law or regulation requires the engagement, in which case the report says so.

why.A: Objectivity does not replace the independence requirement.
why.B: A statement of nonindependence is permitted only when law or regulation requires the engagement.
why.C: Independence is required in attestation engagements, including agreed-upon procedures.
why.D: Correct. The practitioner must be independent unless required by law or regulation to accept the engagement, in which case the report states the lack of independence.

verify.note: 풀이자는 B 를 골랐음(AT-C 215 를 잘못 기억: 비독립 시 보고서에 명시하면 된다고 봄). 검색 결과로 SSAE 19 는 법·규정이 수임을 요구하는 경우를 제외하면 독립성을 요구한다고 확인, 정답 D 유효(풀이자 실수).

guide.ask: Is independence required for an agreed-upon procedures engagement?
guide.reveal: Yes, unless law or regulation requires acceptance of the engagement.

guide.ask: What if not required by law?
guide.reveal: The CPA may not perform it while not independent.

items.blueprint: AUD.IV.C Accounting and review service engagements [IV.C.1]
items.topic: Reporting on a preparation engagement
items.task: Identify the considerations for preparation engagements.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: Accountant Yu is engaged to prepare financial statements for a small client. She is not engaged to audit, review or compile them. What must she do regarding assurance?
options: Nothing, because no report is issued in a preparation engagement and no assurance is given
Issue a compilation report that describes the procedures she performed on the client's records
Include a no-assurance statement on each page, or else disclaim, compile, or withdraw
Issue a review report expressing limited assurance on the financial statements
items.rule_line: Prepared statements carry a no-assurance statement on each page (or a disclaimer), otherwise compile or withdraw.

why.A: A no-assurance statement is required even though a report is not issued.
why.B: A compilation report is issued only when a compilation engagement is performed.
why.C: Correct. The accountant ensures a no-assurance statement appears on each page; if that cannot be done, she disclaims, compiles or withdraws.
why.D: A review report requires a review engagement and independence.

guide.ask: Does a preparation engagement provide any assurance?
guide.reveal: No, but the accountant must not let the statements imply otherwise.

guide.ask: What is the required step?
guide.reveal: A no-assurance statement on each page; if that cannot be done, disclaim, compile or withdraw.

items.blueprint: AUD.IV.C Accounting and review service engagements [IV.C.2]
items.topic: Content of a compilation report
items.task: Identify factors for reporting on compilation engagements.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: An accountant completes a compilation of the financial statements of Larkin Bakery under the accounting and review standards. Which statement must appear in the compilation report?
options: That the accountant did not audit or review the statements and provides no opinion, conclusion or assurance
That the accountant is independent of the entity under the AICPA Code
That the accountant performed limited procedures and is not aware of any material modifications to make
That the accountant expresses an opinion on whether the statements are presented fairly
items.rule_line: A compilation report disclaims any opinion, conclusion or assurance.

why.A: Correct. The compilation report states that no audit or review was performed and that no opinion, conclusion or assurance is provided.
why.B: Independence is not required for a compilation; a lack of independence is disclosed if it exists.
why.C: That describes the conclusion in a review report.
why.D: A compilation does not provide an opinion.

guide.ask: What does a compilation report say about work performed and assurance?
guide.reveal: That no audit or review was performed.

guide.ask: What else?
guide.reveal: That no opinion, conclusion or assurance is provided.

items.blueprint: AUD.IV.C Accounting and review service engagements [IV.C.2]
items.topic: Compilation when the accountant is not independent
items.task: Identify factors for reporting on compilation engagements.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: Accountant Kim performs a compilation of the financial statements of Larkin Bakery, in which she owns a 10% interest. Which is required?
options: Decline the engagement, because independence is required for a compilation
Say nothing about independence, because a compilation gives no assurance
Indicate the lack of independence in a final paragraph of the report
Issue a review report instead, because a review permits a lack of independence
items.rule_line: In a compilation, a lack of independence is stated in the report's final paragraph.

why.A: Independence is not a requirement for a compilation, so Kim need not decline it.
why.B: The lack of independence must be indicated in the report.
why.C: Correct. A compilation may be performed by an accountant who is not independent, if the report indicates the lack of independence in a final paragraph.
why.D: A review requires the accountant to be independent.

guide.ask: Is independence required for a compilation?
guide.reveal: No, an accountant who is not independent may compile.

guide.ask: What must the report show?
guide.reveal: The lack of independence, in a final paragraph.

items.blueprint: AUD.IV.C Accounting and review service engagements [IV.C.3]
items.topic: Assurance and independence in a review engagement
items.task: Identify factors for reporting on review engagements.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: An accountant is engaged to review the financial statements of Halden Motors, a nonissuer, under the accounting and review standards. Which statement about the engagement is correct?
options: The accountant obtains reasonable assurance through analytical procedures and inquiries, and must be independent of the entity
The accountant obtains limited assurance, mainly through analytical procedures and inquiries, and must be independent
The accountant obtains limited assurance, and independence is not required for a review
The accountant obtains no assurance and independence is not required
items.rule_line: A review gives limited assurance through analytical procedures and inquiries and requires independence.

why.A: Reasonable assurance is the level provided by an audit, not a review.
why.B: Correct. A review provides limited assurance, mainly through analytical procedures and inquiries, and requires independence.
why.C: Independence is required for a review, unlike a compilation.
why.D: A review provides limited assurance, not none.

guide.ask: What assurance does a review provide?
guide.reveal: Limited assurance, mainly through analytical procedures and inquiries.

guide.ask: Is independence required?
guide.reveal: Yes.

items.topic: Reports in a single audit
items.task: Report on compliance in an audit of an entity receiving federal awards.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: Which set of reports and schedules must the auditor's reports in a single audit of a local government include under the Uniform Guidance?
options: An opinion on the financial statements and a report on internal control over financial reporting only, with no report on major programs
An opinion on the financial statements, a GAGAS report on internal control and compliance, and a report on compliance for each nonmajor program, without a findings schedule
An opinion on the financial statements only, with compliance with major program requirements addressed in the notes to the financial statements
An opinion on the statements and schedule, a GAGAS report on internal control and compliance, major program compliance reports, and a findings schedule
items.rule_line: A single audit report package covers the statements, GAGAS internal control and compliance, major program compliance, and findings.

why.A: Compliance reporting for major programs and the schedule of findings are also required.
why.B: The compliance opinions are for major programs, not nonmajor programs.
why.C: A report on major program compliance is required in addition to the statement opinion.
why.D: Correct. The reports must cover the statements and the schedule, internal control and compliance under GAGAS, major program compliance and internal control, and the schedule of findings.

guide.ask: Which reports does a single audit require?
guide.reveal: Financial statement and schedule opinion, a GAGAS report on internal control and compliance, major program compliance and internal control reports.

guide.ask: What else accompanies them?
guide.reveal: A schedule of findings.

items.topic: Likely questioned costs in forming a compliance opinion
items.task: Report on compliance in an audit of an entity receiving federal awards.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: In a compliance audit of a major program at Cedar County, the auditor finds known questioned costs of $18,000 for allowable costs. Projecting a sample gives likely questioned costs of $210,000, and the materiality level for that compliance requirement is $150,000. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: Evaluate only the known questioned costs of $18,000, which are below materiality, and issue an unmodified opinion on compliance
Exclude questioned costs from the evaluation and rely on management's corrective action plan for the program
Evaluate likely as well as known questioned costs; likely costs exceed materiality, so consider modifying the opinion
Modify the opinion on the financial statements rather than the opinion on compliance for the program
items.rule_line: Compliance opinions consider likely questioned costs, not only known questioned costs.

why.A: The auditor must evaluate likely questioned costs, not just known questioned costs.
why.B: A corrective action plan does not replace the auditor's evaluation of noncompliance for the audit period.
why.C: Correct. In forming a compliance opinion, the auditor evaluates likely questioned costs as well as known questioned costs.
why.D: The compliance opinion, not the financial statement opinion, addresses noncompliance with program requirements.

guide.ask: Which questioned costs are evaluated in forming the compliance opinion?
guide.reveal: Both known and likely questioned costs.

guide.ask: Compare the likely amount with the materiality level.
guide.reveal: $210,000 exceeds $150,000, so consider modifying the opinion.

items.topic: Reporting a change in accounting principle
items.task: Report on consistency of financial statements.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: Marlow Co., a nonissuer, changed its inventory method from FIFO to average cost. The auditor concludes that the new method is acceptable and preferable, is properly accounted for and disclosed, and has a material effect. How should the auditor report?
options: Include no paragraph, because the change is adequately disclosed in the notes to the financial statements
Express an adverse opinion because the statements are not comparable between the two periods presented
Express a qualified opinion because of the inconsistency in accounting principle between the periods presented
Add an emphasis-of-matter paragraph describing the change and referring to the disclosure; opinion unmodified
items.rule_line: A justified, properly disclosed, material change in principle requires an emphasis-of-matter paragraph.

why.A: A material change in principle requires the emphasis paragraph even when it is disclosed.
why.B: An adverse opinion would apply only for a material and pervasive misstatement.
why.C: A justified, properly disclosed change does not require a qualified opinion.
why.D: Correct. When the criteria are met and the effect is material, the auditor adds an emphasis-of-matter paragraph on the change.

guide.ask: Is the change in principle acceptable, preferable and properly disclosed?
guide.reveal: Yes, and the effect is material.

guide.ask: How does the report reflect it?
guide.reveal: An emphasis-of-matter paragraph on the change, referring to the disclosure, with the opinion unmodified.

items.topic: Responsibility for other information
items.task: Report on other information in documents containing audited financial statements.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: Whitcomb Steel, a nonissuer, includes a letter from the CEO and a discussion of results in an annual report containing audited financial statements. What is the auditor's responsibility for this other information?
options: Read it, consider material inconsistencies with the statements, and stay alert for misstatements of fact
Search for omitted information to determine that the other information is complete and accurate
Audit the other information and express an opinion on it, in addition to the opinion on the statements
None, because the auditor's opinion covers only the audited financial statements themselves
items.rule_line: The auditor reads and considers other information for inconsistency but does not audit it.

why.A: Correct. The auditor reads the other information, considers material inconsistencies, and remains alert for inconsistencies with the auditor's knowledge and misstatements of fact.
why.B: The auditor is not responsible for searching for omitted information or for its completeness.
why.C: The auditor does not audit other information or express an opinion on it.
why.D: The auditor has responsibilities for reading and considering other information even though the opinion covers only the financial statements.

guide.ask: What is the auditor's duty for other information in the annual report?
guide.reveal: Not to audit it or search for omissions.

guide.ask: What does the auditor do with it?
guide.reveal: Read it, consider material inconsistencies with the statements and remain alert for misstatements of fact.

items.topic: Supplementary information in relation to the financial statements
items.task: Report on supplementary information.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: Pine Ridge Farms, a nonissuer, presents a supplementary schedule of production costs with its audited financial statements, and the auditor is engaged to report on whether it is fairly stated in relation to the financial statements as a whole. Which condition must be met?
options: The supplementary information must cover a different period from the financial statements
It was derived from, and relates directly to, the accounting records used to prepare the statements
The auditor's report on the financial statements must contain an adverse opinion or disclaimer
The auditor must audit the supplementary information separately using a lower materiality level
items.rule_line: Supplementary information must derive from the accounting records, cover the same period, and be assessed with the audit's materiality level.

why.A: The supplementary information must relate to the same period as the financial statements.
why.B: Correct. One condition is that the supplementary information was derived from and relates directly to the underlying accounting records used for the statements.
why.C: The report on the financial statements must contain neither an adverse opinion nor a disclaimer.
why.D: The auditor uses the same materiality level as in the audit of the financial statements.

guide.ask: What must be true of supplementary information for an in-relation-to opinion?
guide.reveal: Its source must connect to the records behind the statements.

guide.ask: Which condition states that?
guide.reveal: It was derived from, and relates directly to, the underlying accounting records used to prepare the statements.

items.topic: Review of interim financial information for an issuer
items.task: Report on review of interim financial information.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: Which statement correctly describes a review of interim financial information performed for an issuer under PCAOB standards?
options: It gives a basis for reporting whether material modifications are needed, but not for an opinion
It applies the same procedures as an audit but to the interim period only, and results in an opinion
It provides a basis for expressing an opinion on the annual financial statements taken as a whole
It includes tests of internal control and confirmations to the same extent as an audit of annual statements
items.rule_line: An interim review is much narrower than an audit and does not support an opinion.

why.A: Correct. The objective of a review is a basis for reporting on whether the accountant is aware of material modifications needed, unlike an audit.
why.B: A review differs significantly from an audit in objective and scope, and does not result in an opinion.
why.C: A review of interim information does not provide a basis for an opinion on the annual statements.
why.D: A review is substantially less in scope than an audit and does not include audit-level testing.

guide.ask: What does a review of interim information support?
guide.reveal: Only reporting on whether modifications are needed, not an opinion.

guide.ask: How does it differ from an audit?
guide.reveal: It has narrower procedures without the tests of controls and confirmations of an audit.

items.topic: Report on financial statements prepared under a special purpose framework
items.task: Report on special purpose frameworks.
items.task_source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints (Approved Aug. 18, 2025; effective Jan. 2026), AUD; wording paraphrased
items.stem: The auditor of Willow Farms, a nonissuer, audits financial statements prepared on the cash basis, which is a special purpose framework, for a lender. What must the auditor's report include in addition to the standard elements?
options: A qualified opinion, because the cash basis statements do not follow generally accepted accounting principles
An adverse opinion on the statements, since the cash basis is not an acceptable financial reporting framework
An emphasis-of-matter paragraph alerting users that the basis of accounting is a special purpose framework
No additional paragraph is needed, because the framework is already described in the notes to the statements
items.rule_line: Reports on special purpose framework statements include an emphasis paragraph alerting users to the basis of accounting.

why.A: A special purpose framework can be acceptable, so departure from GAAP alone does not require a qualified opinion.
why.B: The cash basis can be an acceptable special purpose framework.
why.C: Correct. Reports on special purpose statements include an emphasis-of-matter paragraph that alerts users, refers to the note, and says the basis is other than GAAP.
why.D: The alerting paragraph is required even when the note describes the framework.

guide.ask: What kind of framework is the cash basis in this report?
guide.reveal: A special purpose framework.

guide.ask: What does the auditor add to alert users?
guide.reveal: An emphasis-of-matter paragraph that refers to the note and says the basis is other than GAAP.
